    def send_payload(self, payload: RobotCommand) -> None:
    if self._panda is None or self._controller is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Franka Panda deployment is not connected.")
    if not self._controller_started:
        # The first payload is the boot STOP hold of the measured pose, so the controller
        # starts with the arm's own pose as its setpoint: no jerk.
        self._panda.start_controller(self._controller)
        self._controller_started = True

    # Low-pass the arm on every path (hold / INIT / policy); the payload carries what is sent. Not
    # the fingers: a filtered width ramps over many ticks, the gripper worker dispatches each step
    # of it as a new command, and every new command stops the one in flight -- a closing grasp
    # would be stopped and re-issued at the control rate (:meth:`_gripper_worker`).
    commanded = np.asarray(payload.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64)
    sent = self._apply_target_lpf(commanded)
    sent[self._finger_dof_indices] = commanded[self._finger_dof_indices]
    payload.dofs_pos = sent
    target_q = self._extract_arm_target(payload.dofs_pos)
    target_q = self._clamp_arm_velocity(target_q)
    self._controller.set_control(target_q)

    # The hold, the INIT ramp and the START tick leave the gripper at the policy's last
    # command: a target from the measured width would stop a force-controlled grasp and
    # re-send it as a plain move, and INIT's default width would open it on what it holds.
    if self._has_gripper and not self.sending_hold:
        self._set_gripper_target(self._extract_target_width(payload.dofs_pos))

    def grasp(self, width: float, force: float | None = None) -> bool:
    """Grasp (synchronously) an object of approximately ``width`` meters.

    Returns ``True`` when the firmware reports the fingers clamped on
    something within the configured tolerance. Sets the background
    gripper worker's target to ``width`` first, so the worker does not
    countermand the grasp with a ``move`` of its own.
    """
    if self._gripper is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Gripper is not configured for this deployment.")
    with self._gripper_command_lock:
        self._gripper_target_width = float(width)
    return bool(
        self._gripper.grasp(
            width=float(width),
            speed=self.gripper_speed,
            force=float(force if force is not None else self.gripper_force),
            epsilon_inner=self.gripper_epsilon_inner,
            epsilon_outer=self.gripper_epsilon_outer,
        )
    )

    RoboTeraXHandDeployment ¶

    RoboTeraXHandDeployment(env: EnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions)

    Bases: DeploymentBase

    Deployment backend for the RoboTera XHand1 dexterous hand.

    Supports both EtherCAT and RS485 communication protocols. For RS485 you must also set serial_port and baud_rate to match your hardware.

    The hand is treated as a fixed-base robot: read_state returns an identity quaternion and zero angular velocity because the hand has no IMU.

    Joint velocity is a finite difference. The SDK's FingerState_t has a position and no velocity, so read_state differences consecutive positions over the wall-clock time between the two reads (monotonic clock). The first read after connect has no previous sample and reports zero. It is a control-period average, not the instantaneous value the simulator reports, so expect it to be noisier and a period late.

    The hand runs its own PD, with the gains below -- not the command's. finger_command carries kp / ki / kd as int16 values in firmware units, which have no known mapping to the N·m/rad of :attr:RobotCommand.dofs_kp (the xhand1 sysid example fits the effective sim-side gains for that reason). So send_payload forwards positions only: RobotCommand.dofs_kp / dofs_kd / dofs_vel / dofs_torque are not sent, and the firmware gains are set once at connect from dofs_kp / dofs_ki / dofs_kd. A payload with kp = 0 therefore changes nothing on the hand. The two base options that work through command gains, deploy_kp_kd_scale and disable_joints, are refused at construction rather than accepted and ignored. Change these options instead. connect logs the gains it programs.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION

    Bus to open. RS485 also needs serial_port and baud_rate.

    RS485 device path.

    def connect(self) -> None:
    if xhand_control is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "xhand_controller package is not installed. Install it before using RoboTeraXHandDeployment."
        )

    self._device = xhand_control.XHandControl()

    if self.protocol == "EtherCAT":
        ports = self._device.enumerate_devices("EtherCAT")
        if not ports:
            raise RuntimeError("No EtherCAT XHand devices found.")
        rsp = self._device.open_ethercat(ports[0])
    elif self.protocol == "RS485":
        rsp = self._device.open_serial(self.serial_port, self.baud_rate)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown protocol '{self.protocol}'. Expected 'RS485' or 'EtherCAT'.")

    if rsp.error_code != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to open XHand device: {rsp.error_message}")

    # Wait until the device enumerates at least one hand, then verify that the
    # configured hand_id is present.  When hand_id is 0 (default) we auto-select
    # the first discovered hand for single-hand setups.
    start_time = time.time()
    while True:
        ids = self._device.list_hands_id()
        if ids:
            if self.hand_id in ids:
                self._active_hand_id = self.hand_id
                break
            if self.hand_id == 0:
                self._active_hand_id = ids[0]
                break
            raise RuntimeError(f"Configured hand_id {self.hand_id} not found. Available hand IDs: {ids}")
        if time.time() - start_time > self.connect_timeout_s:
            raise RuntimeError("Timed out waiting for XHand device to enumerate hand IDs.")
        time.sleep(0.05)

    self._hand_cmd = xhand_control.HandCommand_t()
    for i in range(_NUM_JOINTS):
        fc = self._hand_cmd.finger_command[i]
        fc.id = i
        fc.kp = self.dofs_kp
        fc.ki = self.dofs_ki
        fc.kd = self.dofs_kd
        fc.position = 0.0
        fc.tor_max = self.tor_max
        fc.mode = self.finger_mode

    # A fresh link has no previous sample: the first read reports zero velocity.
    self._prev_dofs_pos = None
    self._prev_read_t = None
    en.logger.info(
        f"[deploy] XHand firmware PD: kp={self.dofs_kp} ki={self.dofs_ki} kd={self.dofs_kd} "
        f"tor_max={self.tor_max} (firmware units, on every finger). RobotCommand gains are not "
        "forwarded; set the dofs_kp / dofs_ki / dofs_kd deployment options to change these."
    )

    def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    if self._device is None:
        raise RuntimeError("XHand deployment is not connected.")

    for attempt in range(self.crc_retries):
        err, state = self._device.read_state(self._active_hand_id, True)
        if err.error_code == 0:
            break
        en.logger.warning(f"read_state CRC error (attempt {attempt + 1}/{self.crc_retries}): {err.error_message}")
    else:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to read XHand state after {self.crc_retries} attempts: {err.error_message}")
    read_t = time.perf_counter()

    dofs_pos = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
    dofs_torque = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)

    joint_diagnostics: list[dict] = []
    for i, finger_idx in enumerate(self._dof_index):
        finger = state.finger_state[finger_idx]
        dofs_pos[i] = finger.position
        dofs_torque[i] = finger.torque
        joint_diagnostics.append(
            {
                "id": finger.id,
                "raw_position": finger.raw_position,
                "sensor_id": finger.sensor_id,
                "temperature": finger.temperature,
                "commboard_err": finger.commboard_err,
                "jonitboard_err": finger.jonitboard_err,
                "tipboard_err": finger.tipboard_err,
            }
        )

    # Collect fingertip tactile data for the five sensor-equipped fingers.
    fingertip_sensors: dict[int, dict] = {}
    for sensor_idx, finger_id in enumerate(_SENSOR_FINGERS):
        sensor_data = state.sensor_data[sensor_idx]
        fingertip_sensors[finger_id] = {
            "calc_pressure": np.array(
                [
                    sensor_data.calc_force.fx,
                    sensor_data.calc_force.fy,
                    sensor_data.calc_force.fz,
                ]
            ),
            "raw_pressure": np.array([[force.fx, force.fy, force.fz] for force in sensor_data.raw_force]),
            "sensor_temperature": sensor_data.calc_temperature,
        }

    dofs_vel = self._finite_difference_dofs_vel(dofs_pos, read_t)

    return RobotState(
        stamp=time.time(),
        # The XHand1 is a fixed-base end-effector with no on-board IMU.
        base_quat=np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),  # identity (wxyz)
        base_ang_vel=np.zeros(3),
        base_lin_acc=np.zeros(3),
        dofs_pos=dofs_pos,
        dofs_vel=dofs_vel,
        dofs_torque=dofs_torque,
        extra={
            "fingertip_sensors": fingertip_sensors,
            "joint_diagnostics": joint_diagnostics,
        },
    )

    def send_payload(self, payload: RobotCommand) -> None:
    if self._device is None or self._hand_cmd is None:
        raise RuntimeError("XHand deployment is not connected.")

    # Low-pass every path (hold / INIT / policy); the payload carries what is sent.
    payload.dofs_pos = self._apply_target_lpf(np.asarray(payload.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64))
    for i, finger_idx in enumerate(self._dof_index):
        fc = self._hand_cmd.finger_command[finger_idx]
        fc.id = finger_idx
        fc.position = float(payload.dofs_pos[i])

    for attempt in range(self.crc_retries):
        err = self._device.send_command(self._active_hand_id, self._hand_cmd)
        if err.error_code == 0:
            break
        en.logger.warning(f"send_command CRC error (attempt {attempt + 1}/{self.crc_retries}): {err.error_message}")
    else:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to send XHand command after {self.crc_retries} attempts: {err.error_message}")

    def set_hand_id(self, new_id: int) -> None:
    """Change the hand ID on the device."""
    if self._device is None:
        raise RuntimeError("XHand deployment is not connected.")
    err = self._device.set_hand_id(self._active_hand_id, new_id)

    Functions:¶

    Wuji Hand¶

    Wuji Hand 1 / Hand 2 real-robot deployment backend.

    Both generations are 20-DOF hands (5 fingers x 4 joints) whose SDKs speak joint angles in radians, finger-major (thumb first), in the MJCF joint directions -- no sign or offset conversion. The SDK order is the same for a right and a left hand; the side is a property of the joint names, which :data:WUJI_JOINT_IDX maps for both sides and both naming schemes in Eden:

    • {right,left}_finger{1..5}_joint{1..4} (:class:~eden.options.robots.wuji_hand1.WujiHand1_R and the wuji-mjlab task models), and
    • {r,l}_{thumb_cmc_flex, ..., pinky_dip} (:class:~eden.options.robots.wuji_hand2beta2.WujiHand2Beta2_R), whose declaration order is the same finger-major order (upstream WUJI_HAND2_TASK_NAMES).

    A :class:HandTransport is the wire to one hand: :class:Hand1Transport (wujihandpy) or :class:Hand2Transport (wuji_sdk). It streams targets the way upstream wuji-mjlab does:

    • "sync" (upstream reorient): :meth:HandTransport.command blocks for one control period, writing servo_hz linearly interpolated sub-targets from the previous command to the new one.
    • "thread" (upstream pen spin): :meth:HandTransport.command starts a new ramp and returns; a background thread streams it at servo_hz and holds the target once the ramp ends.

    :class:WujiHandDeployment drives one hand through a transport it builds at :meth:connect, or one handed to it with :meth:WujiHandDeployment.use_transport (a simulator, for sim-to-sim).

    def __init__(self, stream: StreamOptions, joint_names: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> None:
    self.stream = stream
    self.joint_names = _SDK_JOINTS if joint_names is None else tuple(joint_names)
    if len(self.joint_names) != NUM_JOINTS:
        raise ValueError(f"joint_names needs the {NUM_JOINTS} joints in SDK order, got {list(self.joint_names)}")
    self._cmd: np.ndarray | None = None
    self._deadline: float | None = None
    self._lock = threading.Lock()
    self._seg_start: np.ndarray | None = None
    self._seg_target: np.ndarray | None = None
    self._seg_t0 = 0.0
    self._servo_thread: threading.Thread | None = None
    self._servo_stop = threading.Event()
    self._servo_error: BaseException | None = None

    def command(self, target: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Stream ``target`` from the previous command, as upstream does for this task."""
    target = _checked(target, self.joint_names)
    if self._cmd is None:
        self._cmd = self.read().copy()
    if self.stream.mode == "sync":
        self._ramp(self._cmd, target, self.stream.interp_s)
        self._cmd = target.copy()
        return
    self._ensure_servo()
    self._set_segment(None, target)
    hold ¶
    hold() -> None

    Let one control period pass with no new target, holding the last one.

    "sync" re-streams the last command across the period through :meth:_ramp, so a tick that sends nothing still lasts one control period (on a simulator's clock too); before any command there is nothing to hold, and it only waits. "thread" returns at once: the servo thread is already holding, and the base rate limiter paces the loop.

    def hold(self) -> None:
    """Let one control period pass with no new target, holding the last one.

    ``"sync"`` re-streams the last command across the period through :meth:`_ramp`, so a tick
    that sends nothing still lasts one control period (on a simulator's clock too); before any
    command there is nothing to hold, and it only waits. ``"thread"`` returns at once: the servo
    thread is already holding, and the base rate limiter paces the loop.
    """
    if self.stream.mode != "sync":
        self._raise_if_servo_failed()
        return
    if self._cmd is None:
        time.sleep(self.stream.interp_s)
        return
    self._ramp(self._cmd, self._cmd, self.stream.interp_s)

    def ease_to(
    self,
    goal: np.ndarray,
    duration_s: float,
    rate_hz: float,
    profile: str,
    guard: Callable[[], None] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Move from the measured pose to ``goal``: upstream's ``home`` (cosine, 100 Hz) or start-pose smoothstep.

    ``guard`` runs before every waypoint, so a safety check that raises stops a multi-second
    move where it is, holding the last waypoint, instead of only before it starts.
    """
    if not (duration_s >= 0.0 and rate_hz > 0.0):
        raise ValueError(f"ease_to needs duration_s >= 0 and rate_hz > 0; got {duration_s!r}, {rate_hz!r}.")
    goal = _checked(goal, self.joint_names)
    start = self.read().copy()
    n = max(1, round(duration_s * rate_hz))
    path = [start + ease(i / n, profile) * (goal - start) for i in range(1, n + 1)]
    if self.stream.mode == "sync":
        for prev, q in zip([start, *path], path):
            if guard is not None:
                guard()
            self._ramp(prev, q, 1.0 / rate_hz)
            self._cmd = q.copy()
        return
    if self._servo_thread is None:
        self._cmd = start
    for q in path:
        if guard is not None:
            guard()
        self._ensure_servo()
        self._set_segment(q, q)
        time.sleep(1.0 / rate_hz)

    def stop_servo(self) -> None:
    self._servo_stop.set()
    if self._servo_thread is not None:
        self._servo_thread.join(timeout=1.0)
        if self._servo_thread.is_alive():
            en.logger.error("[wuji] servo thread did not stop within 1 s; disconnecting anyway")
    self._servo_thread = None

    Wuji Hand 1 via wujihandpy's realtime position controller (upstream WujiHand1Driver).

    The hand runs its own position loop behind a low-pass; command gains do not apply.     def connect(self) -> None:
    self._stale = None
    try:
        import wujihandpy
    except ImportError as e:
        raise ImportError(
            "Wuji Hand 1 needs wujihandpy (upstream pins 1.5.1): pip install wujihandpy==1.5.1"
        ) from e
    self._hand = wujihandpy.Hand()
    self._hand.write_joint_effort_limit(float(self.effort_limit_a))
    # Energized from here on: any failure must de-energize before propagating.
    try:
        self._hand.write_joint_enabled(True)
        self._ctrl_cm = self._hand.realtime_controller(
            enable_upstream=True, filter=wujihandpy.filter.LowPass(cutoff_freq=float(self.lowpass_cutoff_hz))
        )
        self._ctrl = self._ctrl_cm.__enter__()
    except BaseException:
        self.disconnect()
        raise
    en.logger.info(
        f"[wuji] Hand 1 enabled: current limit {self.effort_limit_a:g} A, target low-pass "
        f"{self.lowpass_cutoff_hz:g} Hz, {self.stream.mode} streaming at {self.stream.servo_hz:g} Hz"
    )

    def read(self) -> np.ndarray:
    try:
        q = self._hand.read_joint_actual_position(timeout=self.stale_after_s)
    except Exception as e:
        self._stale = (
            f"read_joint_actual_position(timeout={self.stale_after_s:g}) failed with "
            f"{type(e).__name__}: {e} (USB link lost?)"
        )
        raise DeployStop(f"hand feedback lost: {self._stale}") from e
    return np.asarray(q, dtype=np.float64).flatten()

    def disconnect(self) -> None:
    try:
        if self._ctrl_cm is not None:
            self._ctrl_cm.__exit__(None, None, None)
    except BaseException as e:
        en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] Hand 1 realtime_controller close failed: {e}")
    finally:
        self._ctrl = self._ctrl_cm = None
    if self._hand is not None:
        try:
            self._hand.write_joint_enabled(False)
        except BaseException as e:
            en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] Hand 1 disable failed: {e}")

    Bases: HandTransport

    Wuji Hand 2 via wuji_sdk (upstream WujiHand2Driver and pen spin's Hand2Compat).

    Connects to serial_number (or the single hand on the bus), programs the MIT gains and the current limit, enables the motors, and streams JointCommand(q, 0, 0). Joint positions arrive on the SDK's joint_states callback; joint_diagnostics feeds :meth:fault, and the age of the joint feed feeds :meth:stale.

    def __init__(
    self,
    stream: StreamOptions,
    gains: Hand2Gains,
    serial_number: str = "",
    require_all_joints: bool = True,
    feedback_timeout_s: float = 2.0,
    stale_after_s: float = 0.5,
    joint_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(stream, joint_names)
    self.gains = gains
    self.serial_number = serial_number
    self.require_all_joints = require_all_joints
    self.feedback_timeout_s = feedback_timeout_s
    self.stale_after_s = stale_after_s
    self.device_name = f"eden_wuji_hand_2_{next(_device_seq)}"
    self._sdk = self._mgr = self._hand = self._pub = self._sub = self._diag_sub = None
    self._state_lock = threading.Lock()
    self._latest = np.zeros(NUM_JOINTS)
    self._joint_t = np.full(NUM_JOINTS, -np.inf)
    self._watched = np.ones(NUM_JOINTS, dtype=bool)
    self._last_state_t = 0.0
    # Every (nid, code) ever reported, in arrival order, never replaced: a joint's later warning must
    # not un-latch the error it reported first. (Insertion-ordered dict: a set would lose the order.)
    self._errors: dict[tuple[int, int], None] = {}
    self._temps: dict[int, float] = {}
    self._dismissed: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()

    def connect(self) -> None:
    from eden.utils.devices.wuji.glove import load_sdk

    self._sdk = wuji_sdk = load_sdk()
    self._mgr = wuji_sdk.SdkManager.instance()
    sn = self.serial_number or self._only_hand_on_the_bus()
    self._hand = self._mgr.connect(
        sn=sn, device_name=self.device_name, options=wuji_sdk.ConnectOptions(enable_bridge=False)
    )
    en.logger.info(f"[wuji] connected Wuji Hand 2 sn={self._hand.serial_number}")
    # Connected from here on: any failure must disable and release the link before propagating.
    try:
        n_online = self._hand.online_joints_count().get()
        if (self.require_all_joints and n_online != NUM_JOINTS) or n_online == 0:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Wuji Hand 2 {sn}: {n_online}/{NUM_JOINTS} joints online; refusing to move an incomplete "
                "hand (a missing joint reads back as its default pose). To run with the joints that are "
                "online, WujiHandDeployment.configure(require_all_joints=False)."
            )
        g = self.gains
        self._hand.effort_limit().set([float(a) for a in g.effort_limit_a])
        self._hand.mit_params().set(
            [wuji_sdk.MitParam(float(p), float(d)) for p, d in zip(g.kp, g.kd, strict=True)]
        )
        self._sub = self._hand.joint_states().subscribe_with_callback(self._on_state)
        try:
            self._diag_sub = self._hand.joint_diagnostics().subscribe_with_callback(self._on_diag)
        except Exception as e:
            en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] joint_diagnostics unavailable ({e}); faults limited to stale feedback")
        self._hand.enable()
        time.sleep(_HAND2_ARM_DELAY_S)
        self._pub = self._hand.joint_command().publish()
        self._await_feedback(n_online)
    except BaseException:
        self.disconnect()
        raise
    partial = "" if self._watched.all() else f", {int(self._watched.sum())}/{NUM_JOINTS} joints online"
    en.logger.info(
        f"[wuji] Hand 2 enabled: kp {min(g.kp):.3g}-{max(g.kp):.3g}, kd {min(g.kd):.3g}-{max(g.kd):.3g}, "
        f"current limit {min(g.effort_limit_a):g}-{max(g.effort_limit_a):g} A, "
        f"{self.stream.mode} streaming at {self.stream.servo_hz:g} Hz{partial}"
    )

    def fault(self) -> str | None:
    for nid, code in list(self._errors):
        if (nid, code) in self._dismissed:
            continue
        i = _nid_index(nid)
        joint = f"joint {self.joint_names[i]!r} (nid={nid})" if i is not None else f"node nid={nid}"
        detail, severity = f"0x{code:04X}", ""
        try:
            d = self._hand.describe_error(code)
            if isinstance(d, dict):
                severity = str(d.get("severity", ""))
                detail = f"0x{code:04X} {d.get('name')} [{severity}] {d.get('desc')} ({d.get('resolution')})"
        except Exception:
            pass  # the bare code is still reported below
        if "warn" in severity.lower():
            en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] {joint} warning {detail}")
            self._dismissed.add((nid, code))
            continue
        return f"{joint} error {detail}"
    return None

    def stale(self) -> str | None:
    now = time.monotonic()
    with self._state_lock:
        ages, last = now - self._joint_t, self._last_state_t
    if (feed_age := now - last) > self.stale_after_s:
        return f"joint_states feed stale for {feed_age:.1f} s (bus or link lost?)"
    if missing := [self.joint_names[i] for i in np.flatnonzero(self._watched & (ages > self.stale_after_s))]:
        return f"joint feedback stale for {missing}"
    return None

    def disconnect(self) -> None:
    if self._hand is None:
        return
    try:
        self._hand.disable()
    except Exception as e:
        en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] Hand 2 disable failed: {e}")
    for sub in (self._diag_sub, self._sub):
        try:
            if sub is not None:
                sub.close()
        except Exception as e:
            en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] Hand 2 subscription close failed: {e}")
    # This connection only: ``disconnect_all`` would also drop a glove or the other hand.
    try:
        self._mgr.disconnect(self.device_name)
    except Exception as e:
        en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] Hand 2 disconnect failed: {e}")
    self._hand = self._pub = self._sub = self._diag_sub = None

    WujiHandDeployment ¶

    WujiHandDeployment(env: EnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions)

    Bases: DeploymentBase

    A Wuji Hand 1 or Hand 2, right or left, on a fixed mount.

    The side comes from the robot's joint names (see :data:WUJI_JOINT_IDX); the deployment DOF order may be any permutation of the 20 joints, and is scattered into the SDK's order on the way out and gathered back on the way in. The hand has no IMU: :meth:read_state reports the mount orientation (the robot's default_root_quat) as the base's.

    Joint velocity is a finite difference of consecutive reads over the transport's clock, like the XHand's (neither SDK reports one), optionally low-passed (vel_lowpass_hz).

    Gains are programmed once at connect, never per command. Hand 2 takes MIT kp / kd (mit_kp / mit_kd, default the payload's nominal gains: the robot's default_dofs_kp / default_dofs_kd times deploy_kp_kd_scale). Hand 1 runs its own position loop and has no gain to set. So disable_joints (which works by zeroing command gains) is refused for both, and deploy_kp_kd_scale / mit_kp / mit_kd for Hand 1.

    Loop order. The base control tick (:meth:DeploymentBase.step, the operator state machine every backend runs) with this backend's hooks: :meth:check_safety first, then the command is sent and the period waited out, then the env's episode clock advances (episode_length_buf: the scene is never stepped here, and action warm-ups and clip clocks read it), then the hand is read and :meth:sync_scene -- the hook a subclass uses to write anything else it observes (a camera-tracked object) into the scene -- runs, and only then do the commands publish (sync_before_commands), so a command that grades the new state sees it this tick. In stream_mode="sync" sending the command is the wait (it streams sub-targets across one control period, as upstream does), so the base's rate limiter is not used on top of it: a tick takes one control period, and the inference time is absorbed into it (each period's deadline is chained from the previous one, as upstream anchors its loop before inference). A tick with nothing to send (action=None before a slot has written targets) holds the last target for the period instead (:meth:HandTransport.hold), so it still lasts one period and the episode clock and the reference cannot race ahead at the speed of the loop.

    Boot, INIT and START. :meth:reset restarts the episode clock and the velocity estimate and boots in STOP, holding the measured pose. The operator's INIT ramps from the pose measured at the press to init_target over init_steps ticks and holds it; START hands the hand to the policy. :meth:check_safety runs before every one of those ticks, and :meth:ease_to runs :meth:check_hand before every waypoint.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    hand

    Hardware generation. None infers it from the robot options (WujiHand1* -> "hand1", WujiHand2Beta2* -> "hand2"); any other robot must set it.

    TYPE: ('hand1', 'hand2') DEFAULT: "hand1"

    serial_number

    Hand 2 to connect; empty connects the only hand on the bus.

    TYPE: str

    stream_mode

    How targets are streamed (see the module docstring).

    TYPE: ('sync', 'thread') DEFAULT: "sync"

    servo_hz

    Rate of the interpolated sub-targets.

    TYPE: float

    effort_limit_a

    Joint current limit, A. None: upstream's defaults, 0.5 (Hand 1) / 1.0 (Hand 2).

    TYPE: float | None

    lowpass_cutoff_hz

    Hand 1's target low-pass cutoff.

    TYPE: float

    mit_kp

    def use_transport(self, transport: HandTransport) -> None:
    """Drive ``transport`` (e.g. a simulator for sim-to-sim) instead of the hardware one :meth:`connect` builds."""
    owner = type(self).__name__
    if self._connected:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{owner}.use_transport must be called before connect().")
    if transport.stream.mode != self.stream_mode:
        kind = type(transport).__name__
        raise ValueError(
            f"{owner}.use_transport: {kind} streams {transport.stream.mode!r}, but the deployment is configured "
            f"with stream_mode={self.stream_mode!r} (which decides whether the base rate limiter paces the loop). "
            f"Build it with the deployment's StreamOptions: {kind}(dep.stream, ...)."
        )
    self._transport = transport

    def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    q = self.from_sdk(self.transport.read())
    t = self.transport.clock()
    if self._prev_q is not None and t > self._prev_t:
        dt = t - self._prev_t
        vel = (q - self._prev_q) / dt
        if self.vel_lowpass_hz:
            a = dt / (dt + 1.0 / (2.0 * np.pi * self.vel_lowpass_hz))
            vel = a * vel + (1.0 - a) * self._vel
        self._vel = vel
    self._prev_q, self._prev_t = q.copy(), t
    return RobotState(
        stamp=t,
        base_quat=self._mount_quat,
        base_ang_vel=np.zeros(3),
        base_lin_acc=np.zeros(3),
        dofs_pos=q,
        dofs_vel=self._vel.copy(),
        dofs_torque=np.zeros(self.num_dofs),
    )

    def ease_to(self, target: np.ndarray, duration_s: float, rate_hz: float, profile: str = "cosine") -> None:
    """Move the hand from its measured pose to ``target`` (deployment DOF order), ``"cosine"`` or ``"smoothstep"``.

    :meth:`check_hand` runs before every waypoint. The eased path is not low-passed (it is smooth
    already), but ``target_lpf`` restarts from ``target``, so the next command filters from where
    the hand was eased to rather than pulling it back toward the target before the ease.
    """
    self.check_hand()
    en.logger.info(f"[wuji] easing the hand to its target over {duration_s:g} s ({profile})")
    target = self._clip(np.asarray(target, dtype=np.float64))
    self.transport.ease_to(self.to_sdk(target), duration_s, rate_hz, profile, guard=self.check_hand)
    if self.target_lpf < 1.0:
        self._lpf_prev = target.copy()

    def sdk_index_map(names: Sequence[str], owner: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """Each of ``names``' index in the SDK's joint array, raising (as ``owner``) unless they cover the 20 once each."""
    index = resolve_dof_index_map(names, WUJI_JOINT_IDX, owner=owner, what="Wuji SDK joint index", hint=_NAMING_HINT)
    if sorted(index) != list(range(NUM_JOINTS)):
        by_index = {i: [n for n, j in zip(names, index) if j == i] for i in sorted(set(index))}
        missing = sorted(set(range(NUM_JOINTS)) - set(index))
        twice = {i: dup for i, dup in by_index.items() if len(dup) > 1}
        raise ValueError(
            f"{owner}: the joints must cover each of the {NUM_JOINTS} Wuji SDK joints once; SDK joints {missing} "
            f"have no joint and {twice} have several (SDK index: joint names). {_NAMING_HINT}"
        )
    return np.asarray(index)

    def ease(x: float, profile: str) -> float:
    """Progress along an :data:`EASE_PROFILES` curve at ``x`` in [0, 1]; 0 and 1 at the ends, zero slope at both."""
    if profile not in EASE_PROFILES:
        raise ValueError(f"ease profile must be one of {EASE_PROFILES}; got {profile!r}.")
    return 0.5 * (1.0 - np.cos(np.pi * x)) if profile == "cosine" else x * x * (3.0 - 2.0 * x)

    Composite rigs¶

    Deploy a composite rig -- an arm with a hand welded on, and kin -- as one robot.

    A composite (:class:~eden.options.entities.CompositeEntityOptions, e.g. :class:~eden.options.robots.FrankaXHand) sits in the task's scene under one name and expands into several entities when the env builds -- the Franka arm as robot, the XHand as hand. Each part is its own piece of hardware with its own SDK, so :class:CompositeDeployment drives each through the backend that part's robot is bound to (:func:resolve_deployment_for) and presents the set as one robot to everything above it: the action manager runs once per tick and its targets are split across the parts, the parts' readings are joined into one :class:RobotState, and one observation is computed from all of them.

    The parts' DOFs are laid end to end parent first -- a welded part always after the part it is welded to, otherwise in the rig's declaration order -- so dofs_name -- the layout of every command, of --disable_joints and of --debug_record -- is the arm's joints followed by the hand's.

    The rig runs the one operator state machine every backend runs (boot in STOP, INIT, START, STOP, KILL), once, for all of its parts: one START hands the whole rig to the policy.

    Each part's wire -- connect, read_state, send_payload, _idle_tick, close -- runs on that part's own thread, every part at once, so a tick's I/O takes as long as its slowest part rather than the sum of them all. The policy tick stays one: the loop waits for every part's reading before it observes, and for every part's send before it moves on.

    A part runs as it does deployed alone: its backend's own option defaults, its own wire, its own hooks. The composite adds the joining and changes nothing on a part. The one thing it cannot keep per part is a backend's loop setting that acts on the env every part shares (sync_before_commands, advances_episode_clock): the rig follows one only when every part does, and otherwise runs the standard loop and says which parts it does not follow.

    Classes¶

    CompositeDeployment ¶

    CompositeDeployment(env: RLEnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions)

    Bases: DeploymentBase

    Drive every part of a composite rig through its own backend, as one robot.

    eden deploy picks this backend for any composite (:func:resolve_deployment_for), so a task whose scene holds robot=FrankaXHand(...) deploys onto a Franka and an XHand with no extra flags, assuming both are connected. Each part with joints gets the backend its robot is bound to (FrankaPandaDeployment, RoboTeraXHandDeployment), constructed against its own scene entity; a part with none (a mount) is not deployed.

    What the composite owns, and the parts do not:

    • The loop and the state machine. One action-manager pass and one observation per tick, and one INIT / START / STOP / KILL state machine for the whole rig: it boots in STOP holding every part's measured pose, INIT ramps every joint, and START hands the whole rig to the policy. The operator's inputs are every part's remote (the Oli's joystick, the G1's) plus one keyboard. :meth:connect, :meth:read_state, :meth:send_payload, _idle_tick and :meth:close run on every part at once, each on the part's own thread, and the loop waits for all of them: a tick's I/O takes as long as its slowest part. The scene sync and the other per-tick hooks (_before_step -- a Wuji hand's safety check -- _prepare_reset) run on the loop's thread, part by part, every welded part after its parent (whatever order entity_parts lists them in), so a welded part's FK reads its parent's fresh pose.
    • The pace. The parts are built with sync=False and the composite's rate limiter paces the loop -- unless a part's send itself waits out the control period (a Wuji hand's default stream_mode="sync", :attr:~DeploymentBase.blocks_for_the_period). Then that part paces the rig, as it paces itself deployed alone, and the rig runs no rate limiter on top; the parts' sends overlap, so two such hands still take one period, not two.
    • The loop settings. A backend's sync_before_commands / advances_episode_clock act on the env every part shares, so they cannot be kept per part: the rig follows one only when every part sets it, and otherwise runs the standard loop -- the order and clock a part without it runs deployed alone -- and warns which parts it does not follow. No part takes on another part's loop.
    • The gains. Commands carry the concatenation of the parts' robot gains, scaled by deploy_kp_kd_scale and zeroed on disable_joints. A part whose robot ignores each command's gains (the Franka's controller, the XHand's and Wuji's firmware) cannot go limp that way, so a disabled joint there is refused. Each part takes the rig's scale unless its parts_options sets its own, and its backend also applies it its own way (a Wuji Hand 2 programs its MIT gains from it) or refuses it (an XHand, anything but 1.0).
    • The base reading. Base orientation, angular velocity and acceleration come from the rig's root part (its primary entity), as does the velocity estimator (estimate_lin_vel), on the rig's feet (a :class:~eden.options.robots.composite.base.HumanoidOptions' feet_links). A welded part's own base pose is read off FK through the weld, not off its (IMU-less) reading.
    • Commands, recording, the motion clock -- everything else :class:DeploymentBase does.

    Every other option of a part's backend keeps its own default, as when the part is deployed alone. Each part also runs the composite's :data:FORWARDED_OPTIONS (no backend changes their defaults); parts_options overrides those, and sets each backend's own options, per part::

    CompositeDeployment.configure(parts_options={
    "robot": {"robot_ip": "172.16.0.2"},
    "hand": {"protocol": "EtherCAT"},
})

    (eden deploy --part_option robot.robot_ip=172.16.0.2 --part_option hand.protocol=EtherCAT.)

    Not supported yet, and refused at construction: a part whose backend overrides a method the composite never calls on a part (step, reset, the hold payload -- anything outside :data:PART_HOOKS), two parts with a joint of the same name, and --mujoco sim-to-sim of a composite.

    def __init__(self, env: RLEnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions) -> None:
    #: The deployed parts, by scene entity name, in rig order. Filled by :meth:`_resolve_dofs`.
    self.parts: dict[str, DeploymentBase] = {}
    self._part_slices: dict[str, slice] = {}
    #: Each part's own thread for its wire calls, started on first use (:meth:`_on_part_threads`).
    self._part_threads: dict[str, _PartThread] = {}
    try:
        super().__init__(env, options)
    except BaseException:
        # The parts swap their own entities as they are built, before the composite's own
        # rollback is armed; put back every one that got that far.
        self._undo_part_swaps()
        raise
    if paced := [name for name, part in self.parts.items() if part.blocks_for_the_period]:
        # Each such part waits out the period in its own send, on its own thread, as it does
        # deployed alone (where it runs no rate limiter either); a limiter on top would add
        # whatever the tick spent outside the send to every period.
        self._rate = None
        en.logger.info(
            f"[deploy] Part(s) {paced} wait out the control period in their own send and pace the rig, as they "
            "pace themselves deployed alone; the rig runs no rate limiter of its own."
        )

    @classmethod
def part_backends(cls, rig: CompositeEntityOptions) -> dict[str, type[DeploymentBase]]:
    """The backend each jointed part of ``rig`` deploys through, parent first.

    Raises as construction would for a part that has none or cannot run inside a rig. ``eden
    deploy`` asks before constructing, to hand a backend-specific flag (``--publish_rate``) to
    the parts that declare it.
    """
    return {name: cls._part_backend(rig, name, options) for name, options in cls._jointed_parts(rig).items()}

    def connect(self) -> None:
    """Connect every part at once. If one fails, the ones that came up are closed again, then it raises."""
    _, errors = self._on_part_threads(lambda name, part: part.connect())
    if errors:
        up = {name: part for name, part in self.parts.items() if name not in errors}
        _, unclosed = self._on_part_threads(lambda name, part: part.close(), up)
        for name, exc in unclosed.items():
            en.logger.error(
                f"[deploy] Could not close part '{name}' ({type(self.parts[name]).__name__}) after a failed "
                f"connect: {exc!r}"
            )
        self._raise_part_error(errors, "connecting")

    def close(self) -> None:
    """Close every part at once, each even if another raises; then raise the first failure."""
    errors: list[BaseException] = []
    try:
        self._teardown_common()
    except Exception as exc:
        errors.append(exc)
    _, failed = self._on_part_threads(lambda name, part: part.close())
    for name, exc in failed.items():
        en.logger.error(f"[deploy] Closing part '{name}' ({type(self.parts[name]).__name__}) failed: {exc!r}")
        errors.append(exc)
    self._stop_part_threads()
    if errors:
        raise errors[0]

    def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    """Read every part at once and join the readings, with the base fields from the base part.

    Each part keeps its own reading as its ``state`` too, which its backend reads back (the
    Franka clamps its next command against it). A part's ``extra`` entries are prefixed with
    the part's name, so ``--debug_record`` keeps them apart.
    """
    states, errors = self._on_part_threads(lambda name, part: part.read_state())
    self._raise_part_error(errors, "reading its state")
    for name, part in self.parts.items():
        part.state = states[name]
    base = states[self._base_name]
    return RobotState(
        stamp=base.stamp,
        base_quat=base.base_quat,
        base_ang_vel=base.base_ang_vel,
        base_lin_acc=base.base_lin_acc,
        dofs_pos=np.concatenate([state.dofs_pos for state in states.values()]),
        dofs_vel=np.concatenate([state.dofs_vel for state in states.values()]),
        dofs_torque=np.concatenate([state.dofs_torque for state in states.values()]),
        extra={f"{name}.{key}": value for name, state in states.items() for key, value in state.extra.items()},
    )

    def send_payload(self, payload: RobotCommand) -> None:
    """Send every part its slice of ``payload`` at once; ``payload.dofs_pos`` then holds what was sent (filtered).

    Each part sends it as the rig does: a hold of the rig is a hold of every part
    (:attr:`~DeploymentBase.sending_hold`), so a Franka part keeps its gripper where the policy left it.
    """
    commands = {
        name: RobotCommand(
            dofs_pos=_slice(payload.dofs_pos, part_slice),
            dofs_vel=_slice(payload.dofs_vel, part_slice),
            dofs_torque=_slice(payload.dofs_torque, part_slice),
            dofs_kp=_slice(payload.dofs_kp, part_slice),
            dofs_kd=_slice(payload.dofs_kd, part_slice),
        )
        for name, part_slice in self._part_slices.items()
    }
    for part in self.parts.values():
        part._sending_hold = self._sending_hold
    try:
        _, errors = self._on_part_threads(lambda name, part: part.send_payload(commands[name]))
    finally:
        for part in self.parts.values():
            part._sending_hold = False
    self._raise_part_error(errors, "sending its command")
    sent = np.array(payload.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64)
    for name, command in commands.items():
        sent[self._part_slices[name]] = command.dofs_pos
    payload.dofs_pos = sent

    def programmed_gains(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None:
    """The programmed gains of every part that runs its own, end to end; ``None`` if one has none in our units.

    A part that takes each command's gains runs no fixed set, so its slice holds what it is
    commanded now; :meth:`command_gain_dofs` tells the two apart.
    """
    kp, kd = [], []
    for name, part in self.parts.items():
        part_slice = self._part_slices[name]
        gains = (
            (self.default_dof_kp[part_slice], self.default_dof_kd[part_slice])
            if part.sends_command_gains
            else part.programmed_gains()
        )
        if gains is None:
            return None
        kp.append(gains[0])
        kd.append(gains[1])
    return np.concatenate(kp), np.concatenate(kd)

    Functions:¶

    MuJoCo sim-to-sim¶

    MuJoCo sim-to-sim deployment backend.

    A :class:~eden.extensions.deployment.base.DeploymentBase whose "robot" is a MuJoCo simulation instead of hardware. It runs the exact deploy control loop (eden.utils.cli.tasks._deploy_control_loop) — policy loading, the RobotStateEntity swap, observation assembly, command terms — but reads state from and writes torques to a MuJoCo model rather than a Unitree DDS wire. That makes it a faithful sim-to-sim harness for validating a Genesis-trained policy against an independent physics engine before it ever touches a real robot.

    Inspired by Unitree's unitree_mujoco bridge (github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_mujoco), which stands up a MuJoCo world speaking the Unitree LowState/LowCmd DDS protocol. This backend takes the simpler, robot-agnostic route: it drives MuJoCo directly (no DDS, no unitree_sdk2py), so it works for any robot Eden can describe — the two Unitree families here (G1, Go2) and anything else with a RobotOptions and a loadable MJCF/URDF. The engine details live in :class:~eden.extensions.deployment.utils.mujoco_sim.MujocoSim; this class is the glue between it and the Eden env.

    Selected at deploy time with eden deploy ... --mujoco (see deploy_task), which overrides the usual robot→backend binding so any task/robot can be routed through MuJoCo.

    Physics can run in lockstep with the control loop (the default: each command advances the simulation exactly one control period, so a rollout is deterministic and a late policy costs nothing) or asynchronously (--async / async_physics=True: the simulation advances on its own thread in wall-clock time, like a robot's controller, so a late policy is late for real). See :class:~eden.extensions.deployment.utils.realtime_physics.RealtimePhysics.

    Attributes¶

    Classes¶

    MujocoDeployment ¶

    MujocoDeployment(env: EnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions)

    Bases: DeploymentBase

    Deploy a policy against a MuJoCo simulation of the robot (sim-to-sim).

    Configurable options (in addition to :class:DeploymentBase's):

    mjcf_path: str | None Explicit model file to load into MuJoCo, bypassing mjcf_source resolution. Point this at any hand-authored MuJoCo scene for one-off sim-to-sim runs. mjcf_source: str Which model to load when mjcf_path is unset (default "eden"):

    - ``"eden"``: the robot's own Genesis training asset (``robot_options.file``).
  Always available; the MuJoCo backend reconstructs armature/floor for it.
- ``"menagerie"``: a community-tuned `MuJoCo Menagerie
  <https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco_menagerie>`_ model (with the
  armature/damping/contact params MuJoCo needs), fetched from an HF dataset — the
  higher-fidelity, more independent sim-to-sim target. Errors if the robot has no
  Menagerie mapping or the download fails. Selected by ``eden deploy --menagerie``.
- ``"auto"``: Menagerie when the robot is mapped and the download succeeds,
  otherwise fall back to the Eden asset. Not reachable from the CLI, which keeps
  the loaded model deterministic.

    menagerie_registry: str HF org for the Menagerie dataset (default "Kashu7100"). menagerie_dataset: str HF dataset name mirroring MuJoCo Menagerie (default "mujoco_menagerie"). sim_dt: float | None MuJoCo integration timestep. None keeps the asset's timestep, or in lockstep, when it does not divide the control period, takes the largest step under it that does. In lockstep each step advances control_dt / sim_dt substeps, so a given sim_dt must divide the control period: one that does not is refused rather than rounded, which would run the physics on a clock ahead of or behind the policy's. integrator: str MuJoCo integrator ("implicitfast" default; also "implicit", "euler", "rk4"). implicitfast keeps a stiff joint PD stable. add_floor: bool Add a ground plane if the model has none (default True). It stands where the scene's ground plane does, raised or tilted alike, with its friction (:func:~eden.extensions.deployment.utils.mujoco_scene.read_floor), but keeps MuJoCo's default solver parameters: the robot's own geoms keep its asset's, and a contact's mix of a Genesis value and a MuJoCo one would be neither engine's. provide_ground_truth_base: bool Feed MuJoCo's exact base position and linear velocity to the observation pipeline (default True). Unlike hardware — where these must be estimated — the simulator knows them, so policies that observe base position / linear velocity work without --estimate_lin_vel. Set False to emulate a hardware-blind base.

    Combining it with ``estimate_lin_vel`` is the useful sim-to-sim rehearsal of the
estimator, not a conflict: the estimate is installed *after* the ground-truth
reading, so it is what the policy observes, while the truth stays alongside it in
``state.extra["base_lin_vel"]`` for the estimate
(``state.extra["base_lin_vel_estimate"]``) to be scored against.

    imu_acc_noise, imu_gyro_noise: float Standard deviation of white noise added to every accelerometer (m/s^2) and gyro (rad/s) reading, per axis. Default 0: MuJoCo's IMU is otherwise exact, which hides how an IMU-driven estimate behaves on hardware. Under estimate_lin_vel an exact accelerometer barely drifts even with no foot contact, so a contact dropout that sends the real robot's estimate to -0.5 m/s stays at 0.03 m/s in sim. Turn these on to rehearse the estimator against a hardware-like IMU. imu_acc_bias, imu_gyro_bias: tuple[float, float, float] Constant bias added to the accelerometer (m/s^2) and gyro (rad/s) readings, body frame. Default zero. imu_noise_seed: int | None Seed for the IMU noise generator, so a noisy run can be repeated. None (default) draws a fresh seed. show_viewer: bool Open MuJoCo's native passive viewer to watch the sim-to-sim rollout. record_video: str | None Write the rollout from the policy's first START on to this mp4, rendered offscreen from MuJoCo (:class:~eden.extensions.deployment.utils.mujoco_video.MujocoVideo: two views, one frame per control tick, a STOP's holds included). Lockstep only. Headless, it needs MUJOCO_GL=egl. gantry: bool Hang the robot from a simulated overhead hoist -- the sim counterpart of the bring-up rig, so a biped can be held upright while a controller is commissioned instead of falling every time control pauses. See :meth:~eden.extensions.deployment.utils.mujoco_sim.MujocoSim.set_gantry for the rope model; it is a tension-only spring-damper to a fixed anchor, attached above the centre of mass so it produces a real restoring torque rather than just cancelling weight.

    Re-rigged on every :meth:`reset` from wherever the robot then stands, so the anchor
follows a re-placed robot instead of yanking it back to the first episode's spot.

    gantry_body: tuple[str, ...] Bodies the ropes are tied to, one rope each. Empty (default) uses the robot's own :attr:~eden.options.entities.RobotOptions.gantry_links_name — the two shoulders for a humanoid that declares them — and falls back to the floating base for a robot that declares none. gantry_attach: tuple[float, float, float] | None Attachment point within each rope's body frame, metres. None (default) picks it from how the robot is rigged: the link origin for declared mount links, which for a shoulder sits on the pitch axis at the top of the torso, or 25 cm up for a single base rope, which needs the height to have any moment arm at all. gantry_height: float | None World height of the anchor. Defaults to 1 m above the attachment point. gantry_step: float Metres the operator's + / - keys move the anchor per press. gantry_draw: bool Draw each rope and the force it is pulling with in the --vis viewer (default on). Seeing the pull is most of the value of a simulated rig: a rope that is quietly carrying the robot looks exactly like a robot that is standing, right up until you unrig it. gantry_force_scale: float Metres of force arrow per newton (default 1e-3, so 1 kN draws as 1 m). gantry_stiffness, gantry_damping: Rope spring-damper, N/m and N.s/m. gantry_slack: float Metres of slack. 0 (default) is taut and holds station; a positive value is a safety tether that does nothing until the robot drops that far. gantry_support: float Scale on the rope force, 0-1. Ramp down to hand weight back to the controller. init_steps: int Control cycles the INIT ramp takes to reach the start pose — the sim-to-sim counterpart of the hardware backends' INIT state, inherited from :class:DeploymentBase along with its default of 250 (5 s at 50 Hz). The ramp runs when the operator presses INIT, or on its own in a headless run. The policy does not drive straight from the reset pose: this backend runs the same INIT/START sequence the robot does. init_target: str Inherited from :class:DeploymentBase; this backend is the one that also accepts "motion_rsi", which places joints and base at the tracked reference's frame 0 on reset. "motion" and "default" are the same joint-space ramps here as on the wire. async_physics: bool Run the simulation on its own thread in wall-clock time (default False). Off, physics advances control_dt / sim_dt substeps inside each send_payload and then waits for the next command, so the control loop's timing has no effect on the rollout -- deterministic, and the right mode for comparing two runs. On, the simulation is the robot: it steps at 1 / sim_dt whether or not a new command has arrived, send_payload only replaces the command it holds, and read_state returns the latest state it has published. A policy that overruns the control period therefore leaves the robot executing its previous command for the overrun, and observes a correspondingly older state -- the behaviour hardware has and lockstep cannot show. Selected by eden deploy --mujoco --async.

    The simulated robot has no command latency. A task's :class:~eden.managers.modifiers.actions.actuators.ActionDelay models the Genesis actuator's latency, and no deployment backend applies it: each command acts from the substep it arrives on. A policy trained against a delay therefore runs here with less latency than it trained with. This matters most for a fixed delay (both ends of the range equal), which the policy expects on every step. --async adds only the control loop's real lateness, not the trained delay. eden inference --async is the run that keeps the delay.

    Being robot-agnostic, this backend knows nothing robot-specific — including the feet the estimate_lin_vel filter needs. It does not have to: the robot declares them itself (RobotOptions.feet_links_name), so eden deploy --mujoco --estimate_lin_vel needs no further flag for any robot that names its feet.

    def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions) -> None:
    super().__init__(env, options)
    # A note, not a check, so it stays out of _resolve_options.
    if self.estimate_lin_vel and self.provide_ground_truth_base:
        en.logger.info(
            "[deploy] MuJoCo sim-to-sim: the policy observes the *estimated* base_lin_vel "
            "(estimate_lin_vel overrides the ground-truth reading); the simulator's truth "
            "rides along in state.extra['base_lin_vel'] for comparison. Set "
            "provide_ground_truth_base=False to also blind the base position."
        )
    self._sim: MujocoSim | None = None
    self._physics: RealtimePhysics | None = None
    # The kd the armature currently folds in (``MujocoSim.set_implicit_damping``); set at connect.
    self._damped_kd: np.ndarray | None = None
    self._viewer = None
    self._video: MujocoVideo | None = None
    self._n_substeps = 1
    self._base_pos0 = np.asarray(self.robot_options.default_root_pos, dtype=np.float64)
    self._base_quat0 = np.asarray(self.robot_options.default_root_quat, dtype=np.float64)
    self._imu_rng = np.random.default_rng(self.imu_noise_seed)

    def connect(self) -> None:
    asset = self._resolve_asset()
    floor = None
    if self.add_floor:
        # The ground's pose and friction; MuJoCo's solver parameters, as the robot's geoms keep the asset's.
        floor = dataclasses.replace(read_floor(self._env), sol_params=None)
    self._sim = self._load_sim(asset, self.sim_dt, floor)
    if self.sim_dt is None and not self.async_physics and not divides(self.control_dt, self._sim.sim_dt):
        # Lockstep ends every tick on a step: an asset's timestep off the control period gives way to
        # the largest under it that divides it, as a composite rig's default does.
        fit = fitting_timestep(self.control_dt, self._sim.sim_dt)
        en.logger.info(
            f"[deploy] MuJoCo sim-to-sim: the asset's timestep {self._sim.sim_dt:g} s does not divide the control "
            f"period {self.control_dt:g} s; running at {fit:g} s, the largest under it that does "
            "(--mujoco_sim_dt sets another)."
        )
        self._sim = self._load_sim(asset, fit, floor)
    say_floor_caveat(self._sim.floor)
    # Genesis integrates the PD damping implicitly (its implicit integrators) or folds kd*dt into
    # the armature (``euler``, RigidEntity.post_build); match that here, or a hand-rolled PD on the
    # zero-armature training MJCF diverges.
    self._fold_implicit_damping()
    if self.async_physics:  # the physics thread keeps its own clock, at 1 / sim_dt
        self._n_substeps = max(1, round(self.control_dt / self._sim.sim_dt))
    else:
        self._n_substeps = steps_per_tick(self.control_dt, self._sim.sim_dt)
    self._sim.reset(self.default_dof_pos, self._base_pos0, self._base_quat0)
    mode = "asynchronous, physics on its own thread" if self.async_physics else "lockstep with the control loop"
    en.logger.info(
        f"[deploy] MuJoCo sim-to-sim: {asset} | sim_dt={self._sim.sim_dt:g}s "
        f"× {self._n_substeps} substeps/step | integrator={self.integrator} | {mode}"
    )
    if self.show_viewer:
        import mujoco.viewer

        self._viewer = mujoco.viewer.launch_passive(self._sim.model, self._sim.data)
    if self.async_physics:
        overlay = self._draw_gantry_overlay if self.gantry and self.gantry_draw else None
        self._physics = RealtimePhysics(
            self._sim, self._hold_default_pose(), viewer=self._viewer, viewer_overlay=overlay
        )
        self._physics.start()
    if self.record_video is not None:
        from eden.extensions.deployment.utils.mujoco_video import MujocoVideo

        self._video = MujocoVideo(
            self._sim.model,
            self._sim.data,
            self.record_video,
            fps=1.0 / self.control_dt,
            framed_bodies=self._sim.robot_body_ids(),
            markers=kinematic_markers(self._env),
        )

    def close(self) -> None:
    if self._physics is not None:
        # Stop the robot's clock before anything else, and let it grade itself: a physics
        # thread that fell behind wall time silently stretched every control period.
        self._physics.stop()
        log = en.logger.warning if self._physics.reanchors else en.logger.info
        log(self._physics.summary())
        self._physics = None
    self._teardown_common()
    if self._video is not None:
        self._video.close()
        self._video = None
    if self._viewer is not None:
        try:
            self._viewer.close()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort on the way down
            pass
        self._viewer = None
    self._sim = None

    def rig_gantry(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
    """Rig or release the gantry mid-run, anchored over where the robot stands now.

    The switch a caller driving its own loop needs to hand the robot's weight back to the
    controller (and to catch it again); ``gantry`` itself only sets how a reset rigs it.
    """
    self.gantry = enabled
    self._rig_gantry()
    if not enabled and self._viewer is not None:
        # Nothing redraws the overlay once the gantry is off; drop the last-drawn ropes.
        self._viewer.user_scn.ngeom = 0

    def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    assert self._sim is not None, "connect() must be called before read_state()."
    if self._physics is not None:
        # The latest state the physics thread published, stamped when it was published:
        # in this mode the state has an age, as a wire's does.
        r = self._physics.read()
        stamp = r["stamp"]
    else:
        r = self._sim.read()
        stamp = time.time()
    extra: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if self.provide_ground_truth_base and not self.robot_options.is_fixed_base:
        # The simulator knows the true base pose/velocity; hand them to the
        # observation pipeline so base-position / base-lin-vel terms work without
        # an estimator (RobotStateEntity yaw-aligns them like any world-frame read).
        extra["base_pos"] = r["base_pos"]
        extra["base_lin_vel"] = r["base_lin_vel"]
    return RobotState(
        stamp=stamp,
        base_quat=r["base_quat"],  # wxyz
        base_ang_vel=self._corrupt_imu(r["base_ang_vel"], self.imu_gyro_noise, self.imu_gyro_bias),  # body (gyro)
        base_lin_acc=self._corrupt_imu(r["base_lin_acc"], self.imu_acc_noise, self.imu_acc_bias),  # specific force
        dofs_pos=r["dofs_pos"],
        dofs_vel=r["dofs_vel"],
        dofs_torque=r["dofs_torque"],
        extra=extra,
    )

    def send_payload(self, payload: RobotCommand) -> None:
    assert self._sim is not None, "connect() must be called before send_payload()."
    # As every hardware backend does on its wire, so a --target_lpf rehearsed here is the one the robot gets.
    payload.dofs_pos = self._apply_target_lpf(np.asarray(payload.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64))
    kp = payload.dofs_kp if payload.dofs_kp is not None else self.default_dof_kp
    kd = payload.dofs_kd if payload.dofs_kd is not None else self.default_dof_kd
    # The armature models the damping Genesis folded in at build from the robot the active slot
    # trained on, so it follows the slot's gains (``default_dof_kd``, which a slot switch ramps
    # through ``set_gains``) -- not a payload's own kd, such as the INIT ramp's
    # ``init_dofs_kd_scale``, which was never part of any training robot.
    refold = not np.array_equal(self.default_dof_kd, self._damped_kd)
    if self._physics is not None:
        # Hand the command to the robot's clock; it takes effect at the thread's next
        # substep, and the physics keeps running whether or not another one follows.
        command = PDCommand.of(payload.dofs_pos, payload.dofs_vel, kp, kd, payload.dofs_torque)
        if not refold:
            self._physics.set_command(command)
            return
        # One exclusive section for both, so no burst runs the new damping with the old
        # command or the old damping with the new one.
        with self._physics.exclusive():
            self._fold_implicit_damping()
            self._physics.set_command(command)
        return
    if refold:
        self._fold_implicit_damping()
    self._sim.step_pd(
        target_pos=payload.dofs_pos,
        target_vel=payload.dofs_vel,
        kp=kp,
        kd=kd,
        tau_ff=payload.dofs_torque,
        n_substeps=self._n_substeps,
    )
    if self._video is not None:
        self._video.tick(self.policy_active, marker_poses(self._env, self._video.markers))
    if self._viewer is not None and self._viewer.is_running():
        if self.gantry and self.gantry_draw:
            self._draw_gantry_overlay(self._viewer)
        self._viewer.sync()

    Functions:¶

    MuJoCo sim-to-sim of a composite rig, through the composite deployment itself.

    eden deploy --mujoco on a scene whose --entity_name is a composite rig (KukaSharpa, FrankaXHand, OliWuji) runs :class:MujocoCompositeDeployment: the very :class:~eden.extensions.deployment.composite.CompositeDeployment that drives the rig's hardware -- one backend per part, each on its own thread, one state machine, the parts' readings joined into one observation -- with every part on a :class:MujocoPartDeployment in place of its hardware backend. The parts share one MuJoCo model of the whole rig (:class:~eden.extensions.deployment.utils.mujoco_rig.MujocoRig) plus the scene's props (a table, a tool), so a manipulation policy acts on a simulated object and observes it.

    The MuJoCo model is assembled from the built Genesis env, so it is the rig the policy trained on:

    • each part's own asset, welded where the env welds it -- the mount read off the env's forward kinematics, not re-derived -- and checked link by link against that kinematics at connect;
    • each part's armature and joint damping as built, its material friction (default_geoms_friction per link), its links' contact solver parameters as built (a set_contact_sol_params startup event included) and gravity compensation;
    • each prop at the pose the env spawned it, with its friction and contact parameters.

    Each tick every part writes its command to the model on its own thread, then the composite steps the physics once for the control period (lockstep, as MujocoDeployment), reads the parts back on their threads, and writes each prop's pose into its env entity -- what a mocap system does on hardware -- before the observation is computed. Where hardware has a camera instead (an AprilTag pose estimate), prop_pos_noise / prop_rot_noise / prop_camera_hz / prop_latency_s make what the policy reads of each free prop one: noisy, late and at the camera's rate (the exact pose stays in the state as <prop>.true_pos / <prop>.true_quat for --debug_record). record_video renders the rollout from MuJoCo, as a single robot's backend does, and the base's policy_seconds ends a headless run. The env is read into the rig's description by :mod:~eden.extensions.deployment.utils.mujoco_scene; this class keeps the lifecycle, the checks and the camera.

    def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    r = self._require_rig().read_part(self.entity_name)
    extra: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if self.provide_ground_truth_base and self._is_free_root():
        extra["base_pos"] = r["base_pos"]
        extra["base_lin_vel"] = r["base_lin_vel"]
    # A welded part has no IMU; its base is read off the forward kinematics through the weld.
    return RobotState(
        stamp=time.time(),
        base_quat=r.get("base_quat", np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])),
        base_ang_vel=r.get("base_ang_vel", np.zeros(3)),
        base_lin_acc=r.get("base_lin_acc", np.zeros(3)),
        dofs_pos=r["dofs_pos"],
        dofs_vel=r["dofs_vel"],
        dofs_torque=r["dofs_torque"],
        extra=extra,
    )

    def send_payload(self, payload: RobotCommand) -> None:
    kp = self.default_dof_kp if payload.dofs_kp is None else payload.dofs_kp
    kd = self.default_dof_kd if payload.dofs_kd is None else payload.dofs_kd
    # Each part low-passes its own slice, as its hardware backend does on its wire (``target_lpf``), and
    # leaves what it sent in the payload, which the composite joins into the rig's (``--debug_record``).
    payload.dofs_pos = self._apply_target_lpf(np.asarray(payload.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64))
    self._require_rig().set_command(
        self.entity_name, payload.dofs_pos, payload.dofs_vel, kp, kd, payload.dofs_torque
    )

    MujocoCompositeDeployment ¶

    MujocoCompositeDeployment(env: RLEnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions)

    Bases: CompositeDeployment

    A composite rig deployed onto MuJoCo: :class:CompositeDeployment with a :class:MujocoPartDeployment per part.

    Options (in addition to :class:CompositeDeployment's):

    sim_dt: float | None MuJoCo timestep. None (default) takes the largest step of at most 2 ms that divides the control period exactly, so each tick advances the physics by exactly one control period. A given one must divide it too (eden deploy --mujoco_sim_dt): one that does not is refused. integrator: str "implicitfast" (default), "implicit", "euler" or "rk4". cone: str Friction cone, "elliptic" (default -- grasps hold far better on it) or "pyramidal". props: tuple[str, ...] | None Scene entities to simulate besides the rig (eden deploy --mujoco_props). None (default) takes every colliding entity of the scene that is not the rig or the ground. Each must be a box primitive or a rigid body loaded from a URDF / MJCF, without joints of its own: only its pose reaches the env, which a mesh file's (MuJoCo cannot load one as a body) or an articulated object's joints would not. Anything else is refused, naming it. A kinematic entity (a goal marker: not simulated, no contacts) is never a prop; record_video draws it. prop_pos_noise, prop_rot_noise: float A camera's error on every free prop's pose the policy reads: per-axis white noise on the position (m, standard deviation), and a rotation about a random axis by a normal angle (rad, standard deviation). Default 0. With either on, the quaternion's sign is random too, as a pose estimator's is. Only what the policy observes changes; MuJoCo's physics does not, and the exact pose stays in the state as <prop>.true_pos / <prop>.true_quat. prop_camera_hz: float | None The camera's frame rate: a free prop's observed pose updates at it and holds between frames, on the simulation's clock (a tick that sends nothing advances neither). None (default): every control tick. prop_latency_s: float How old a frame is when it arrives, rounded half up to whole control ticks (with a warning when that changes it). Default 0. prop_noise_seed: int | None Seed for the camera model's noise, so a run can be repeated. None draws a fresh one. record_video: str | None Write the rollout from the policy's first START on to this mp4, rendered offscreen from MuJoCo (two views side by side, one frame per control tick, a STOP's holds included so the video never skips). Headless, it needs MUJOCO_GL=egl. kinematics_tolerance: float Largest link-pose disagreement (metres plus radians) between the MuJoCo model and the env's forward kinematics accepted at connect. Above it the assembly is wrong and connect raises. show_viewer: bool Open MuJoCo's passive viewer on the rig.

    def __init__(self, env: RLEnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions) -> None:
    super().__init__(env, options)
    self._rig: MujocoRig | None = None
    self._viewer = None
    self._n_substeps = 1
    self._damped_kd: np.ndarray | None = None
    # The yaw the props were last written into the env under (the env spawned them under none).
    self._props_yaw = 0.0
    self._prop_names = self._resolve_props()
    # Where each prop spawned, captured before any tick writes the simulated pose over it.
    self._prop_home = {name: entity_pose(self._env, name) for name in self._prop_names}
    self._camera = _PropCamera(
        pos_noise=self.prop_pos_noise,
        rot_noise=self.prop_rot_noise,
        hz=self.prop_camera_hz,
        latency_ticks=self._latency_ticks(),
        control_dt=self.control_dt,
        seed=self.prop_noise_seed,
    )
    self._video: MujocoVideo | None = None
    # Control periods the physics has advanced since the reset: the camera's clock.
    self._sim_ticks = 0

    def connect(self) -> None:
    from eden.extensions.deployment.utils.mujoco_rig import MujocoRig

    # The largest step of at most 2 ms that divides the control period, unless one is given.
    sim_dt = fitting_timestep(self.control_dt, 0.002) if self.sim_dt is None else float(self.sim_dt)
    self._rig = MujocoRig(
        self._rig_parts(),
        rig_props(self._env, {name: self._prop_home[name] for name in self._prop_names}),
        sim_dt=sim_dt,
        integrator=self.integrator,
        cone=self.cone,
        floor=read_floor(self._env),
    )
    say_floor_caveat(self._rig.floor)
    self._check_kinematics()
    self._check_contact_floor()
    self._n_substeps = steps_per_tick(self.control_dt, self._rig.sim_dt)
    for part in self.parts.values():
        part.bind(self._rig)
    super().connect()
    self._reset_sim()
    en.logger.info(
        f"[deploy] MuJoCo rig sim-to-sim: parts {list(self.parts)}, props {self._prop_names} | "
        f"sim_dt={self._rig.sim_dt:.6g}s x {self._n_substeps} substeps/step | integrator={self.integrator} | "
        f"cone={self.cone} | lockstep with the control loop"
    )
    if self.show_viewer:
        import mujoco.viewer

        self._viewer = mujoco.viewer.launch_passive(self._rig.model, self._rig.data)
    if self.record_video is not None:
        from eden.extensions.deployment.utils.mujoco_video import MujocoVideo

        # Framed on the rig's bodies and its free props where they start.
        rig = self._rig
        framed = [rig.prop_body_id(name) for name, prop in rig.props.items() if prop.free] + rig.part_body_ids()
        self._video = MujocoVideo(
            rig.model,
            rig.data,
            self.record_video,
            fps=1.0 / self.control_dt,
            framed_bodies=framed,
            markers=kinematic_markers(self._env),
        )

    def close(self) -> None:
    try:
        super().close()
    finally:
        if self._video is not None:
            self._video.close()
            self._video = None
        if self._viewer is not None:
            try:
                self._viewer.close()
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort on the way down
                pass
            self._viewer = None

    def send_payload(self, payload: RobotCommand) -> None:
    """Every part writes its command (each on its thread), then the physics advances one control period."""
    if self._rig is None:
        raise RuntimeError("MujocoCompositeDeployment: connect() must be called before send_payload().")
    if not np.array_equal(self.default_dof_kd, self._damped_kd):
        self._fold_implicit_damping()
    super().send_payload(payload)
    self._rig.step(self._n_substeps)
    self._sim_ticks += 1
    if self._viewer is not None and self._viewer.is_running():
        self._viewer.sync()
    if self._video is not None:
        self._video.tick(self.policy_active, marker_poses(self._env, self._video.markers))

    def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    state = super().read_state()
    for name in self._prop_names:
        pos, quat = self._rig.prop_pose(name)
        if self._rig.props[name].free and not self._camera.exact:
            # What the policy reads is the camera's; the exact pose stays beside it for a post-mortem.
            state.extra[f"{name}.true_pos"], state.extra[f"{name}.true_quat"] = pos, quat
            pos, quat = self._camera.observe(name, self._sim_ticks, pos, quat)
        state.extra[f"{name}.pos"] = pos
        state.extra[f"{name}.quat"] = quat
    return state

    The MuJoCo world itself (MujocoSim, MujocoRig, the MujocoFloor both add), what both MuJoCo backends read off the built env (mujoco_scene.py), the offscreen recording (MujocoVideo, mujoco_video.py), the Eden-robot-to-Menagerie map (menagerie_path_for), the state and command dataclasses (RobotState, RobotCommand) and the loop helpers (RateLimiter, StreamingRecorder, LinVelKalmanEstimator) live in eden/extensions/deployment/utils/, which has no __init__.py, so they are not rendered here; read them in the source.
